newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares rise sharply in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares rise sharply in active trade.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index rose sharply on Thursday morning in active trading with sentiment much improved following Wednesday's rise, brokers said.
The index advanced 0.993 points or 1.57 percent to 64.160 points, on volume of 8.8 million shares worth $4.1 million, against $2.1 million on Wednesday morning.

Brokers said the breach of the key 63-point resistance level triggered some follow-up buying, with investors encouraged by rumours that there would be good news from an ongoing meeting about the B share markets in Nanjing.

"Rumours that the Nanjing meeting will come up with some positive news helped push the index up," one broker said, adding that a strong performance by market giant Shanghai Tyre also contributed to the rises."
Shanghai Tyre performed strongly on expectations of improved results. It gained $0.022 or 4.7 percent to $0.490 on volume of 470,400 shares.
"Technical charts, which improved after yesterday's rises, indicated the index will rise further in the short term," a second broker said. "We see it hitting 68 points in the short term."
Of 43 B shares, 36 traded, with 30 up and six flat.
Hua Xin Cement was the most active share, rising on institutional buying by $0.016 or 6.15 percent to $0.276 on volume of 831,000 shares.
Shanghai's A share market consolidated up on a strong performance in the Shenzhen bourse, and brokers expected this trend to continue, depending on Shenzhen's movement in the short term.

The index gained 3.982 points or 0.4 percent to 988.060 points on volume of 153 million shares worth 1.6 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index inched up 12.617 points or 0.49 percent to 2564.797 points.
Xiamen Titan was the star on improved results expectations, jumping 0.47 yuan or 8.2 percent to 6.20 yuan on volume of 655,875 shares.
